decision_table.name: Determine_IA_Filing_Requirement
decision_table.description: Determine if corporation must file Iowa state corporate tax return. Checks for physical presence or economic nexus.

condition.name: has_physical_presence
condition.comment: Has physical presence in IA (office, employees, property)

actions.action: // Physical nexus established - filing required // Apportionment will be calculated by tables 7000-7500

rule.policy:
IA filing required due to physical presence (office, employees, or property in state).
A corporation has physical presence nexus in IA if it has: - An office, store, warehouse, or other place of business in IA - Employees working in IA - Tangible personal property located in IA - Real property located in IA
Reference: Iowa Code § 422.32 (Nexus and apportionment) Reference: Iowa Department of Revenue guidance on corporate nexus standards

actions.action: // Economic nexus established per Wayfair - filing required // Apportionment will be calculated by tables 7000-7500

rule.policy:
IA filing required due to economic nexus (post-Wayfair).
Economic nexus threshold: $100,000 gross receipts in IA.
Note: As of July 1, 2023, Iowa eliminated the transaction count threshold (formerly 200 transactions). Only the revenue threshold applies.
Following South Dakota v. Wayfair, Inc., 138 S. Ct. 2080 (2018), IA requires filing if a corporation exceeds economic nexus threshold, even without physical presence.
Reference: South Dakota v. Wayfair, Inc., 138 S. Ct. 2080 (2018) Reference: Iowa Department of Revenue Economic Nexus Guidance Reference: https://revenue.iowa.gov/taxes/tax-guidance/sales-use-excise-tax/remote-sellers-marketplace-facilitators

No IA nexus - no filing requirement.
Corporation does not meet physical presence or economic nexus thresholds. Any estimated payments would be refunded.
Reference: Iowa Code § 422.32 (Nexus requirements)

decision_table.name: Calculate_IA_Income_Adjustments
decision_table.description: Calculate IA state-specific additions and subtractions to federal taxable income.

condition.name: has_nexus
condition.comment: Must have nexus to calculate adjustments

rule.policy:
IA state-specific income adjustments to federal taxable income.
IA ADDITIONS to federal taxable income include: - State income taxes deducted on federal return - Expenses related to exempt income - Interest expense adjustments (IA does not conform to federal IRC § 163(j) limitation) - Certain depreciation adjustments
IA SUBTRACTIONS from federal taxable income include: - Interest on U.S. government obligations (U.S. Treasury bonds, notes, bills) Exempt under 31 USC § 3124(a) - Interest on Iowa state and municipal bonds (listed in Iowa Administrative Code rule 701-302.3) - Iowa net operating loss deduction (subject to IA limitations) - Federal income taxes paid (certain entities only) - Certain dividend income eligible for Iowa dividend received deduction
Reference: Iowa Form IA 1120 (Corporation Income Tax Return) Reference: Iowa Department of Revenue Corporate Income Tax Instructions 2025 Reference: Iowa Code § 422.35 (Adjustments to federal taxable income) Reference: https://revenue.iowa.gov/media/4372/download (2025 IA 1120 Instructions)

No nexus - no state adjustments calculated.
Corporation does not have IA nexus, so no income adjustments are needed.

decision_table.name: Calculate_IA_State_Tax
decision_table.description: Calculate IA state corporate income tax. Applies IA graduated rates (5.5% up to $100K, 7.1% over $100K) to apportioned and adjusted taxable income.

condition.name: has_nexus
condition.comment: Must have nexus to owe tax

rule.policy:
IA state corporate income tax calculation (income over $100,000):
1. Federal taxable income: [Form 1120 line 28] 2. Apportioned to IA: × [IA apportionment percentage] 3. IA additions: + [State taxes, exempt income expenses, etc.] 4. IA subtractions: - [Federal interest, IA municipal interest, IA NOL, etc.] 5. IA taxable income: = [Result] 6. IA tax bracket 1: $100,000 × 5.5% = $5,500 7. IA tax bracket 2: [Income over $100K] × 7.1% 8. Total IA income tax: = [Bracket 1 + Bracket 2] 9. IA credits: - [Research, high quality jobs, renewable energy, historic preservation, etc.] 10. IA tax liability: = [Final tax]
IA uses single-sales factor apportionment (100% sales factor).
IA tax rate structure (2025): - 5.5% on taxable income up to $100,000 - 7.1% on taxable income over $100,000
Note: Iowa is transitioning toward a flat 5.5% rate in future years.
IA provides various tax credits including: - Research activities credit - High quality jobs program credit - Renewable energy tax credit - Historic preservation tax credit - Redevelopment tax credit
Reference: Iowa Form IA 1120 (Corporation Income Tax Return) Reference: Iowa Code § 422.33 (Tax rates) Reference: Iowa Code § 422.32 (Single-sales apportionment) Reference: https://revenue.iowa.gov/taxes/tax-guidance/business-income-tax/iowa-corporate-income-tax-rates

IA state corporate income tax calculation (income $100,000 or less):
1. Federal taxable income: [Form 1120 line 28] 2. Apportioned to IA: × [IA apportionment percentage] 3. IA additions: + [State taxes, exempt income expenses, etc.] 4. IA subtractions: - [Federal interest, IA municipal interest, IA NOL, etc.] 5. IA taxable income: = [Result, $100,000 or less] 6. IA tax: [IA taxable income] × 5.5% 7. IA credits: - [Research, high quality jobs, renewable energy, etc.] 8. IA tax liability: = [Final tax]
For taxable income of $100,000 or less, only the 5.5% rate applies.
Reference: Iowa Form IA 1120 (Corporation Income Tax Return) Reference: Iowa Code § 422.33 (Tax rates) Reference: https://revenue.iowa.gov/taxes/tax-guidance/business-income-tax/iowa-corporate-income-tax-rates

No IA nexus - no tax liability.
Corporation does not have physical presence or economic nexus in IA. Any estimated payments are refunded.
Reference: Iowa Code § 422.32 (Nexus requirements)

No IA taxable income - no tax liability.
Corporation has IA nexus but no positive taxable income after apportionment and adjustments. Any estimated payments are refunded.
IA net operating loss (NOL) rules may apply: - IA allows NOL carryforward (subject to state limitations) - NOL carryback provisions may apply depending on tax year - Consult Iowa Code § 422.35 for specific NOL rules
Reference: Iowa Form IA 1120 (Corporation Income Tax Return) Reference: Iowa Code § 422.35 (Net operating loss deduction)
